title: The Strangest Thing on the Tide Line

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — NATURE, ECOLOGY AND ANIMALS (NAT-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Isola's animals, plants, tides and weather: tide pools and nesting beaches, washed-up rubbish, shrinking clam beds, strange visitors, creatures doing what creatures do, and choices about the island where nobody gets a perfect answer.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a child aged 5-13 and an adult)

collection.description: A child is poking a strange white puffy thing on the tide line: explain and bury it, or let the child guess what it is.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has found something on the beach and is poking it with a stick. It's white, puffy and shaped a bit like a pair of short pants, made of something soft that isn't cloth and isn't leaf. (friend) comes over, takes one look, and makes a face. The older villagers have seen these wash up before. They are called diapers, and they are what they look like.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Somebody, somewhere, wrapped a baby in this," says (friend). "And then it went in the sea." (subject) is delighted and disgusted in equal measure. They carry it a long way up the beach on the end of the stick and bury it deep, far from the water and the gardens. (subject) has a hundred questions about the people who use them. (friend) has no answers to any of them.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) guesses it's a hat. Then a bag. Then a very small boat. (friend) finally tells (subject.him/her). (subject) screams and drops the stick. Then (subject.he/she) laughs so hard (subject.he/she) has to sit down in the sand. They bury it together, well away from the water, and (subject) tells every single child in the village by sunset.
